summary: 76 grade-3 rows re-graded against the primary sources. Everything was read from a fetched document: local PMC JATS for O'Rourke 2026 (PMC12865454), Bravo-Hernandez 2026 (PMC12867516), Kuroda 2025 (PMC12744863), Hagedorn 2022 (PMC9221153), Moazami 2024 (PMC11638874) and the KCNT1 Nature Medicine report (PMC13099374); the O'Rourke and Bravo-Hernandez supplement PDFs; the Hagedorn 148-ASO supplementary xlsx; the Korte 2020 abstract via NCBI E-utilities; the TEGSEDI SPL via DailyMed; the Qalsody and Spinraza SmPCs and the local Qalsody EPAR; the MHRA Drug Safety Update of 25 September 2018 via gov.uk; and PMC copies of Lovett 2025, the BioDrugs HD review and the N=1 Collaborative review. systematic_issues:
1. THE DOMINANT ERROR REPEATS, AND ITS FINGERPRINT IS AN EXPLICIT NUMERIC MAPPING IN THE NOTES. 23 of the 33 downgrades come from acute behavioural scales whose cutoff was set at a fraction of the numeric range instead of at the scale's own text. The extractor wrote the rule into the rows, which makes it greppable: 'Grade mapping for this 0-7 ICV scale: 0->0; 0<s<2->1; 2<=s<4->2; s>=4->3' (O'Rourke ICV), 's>=3->3 (paresis/paralysis)' (O'Rourke IT) and 's>=5->3 (author-defined severe)' (Bravo-Hernandez). Anchored to the published scale text the correct thresholds are: O'Rourke rodent ICV - grade 3 begins at 6, 'No response to tail pinch but still breathing' (7 = Death); 4 is 'Any movement after lift' and 5 is 'Lateral recumbency with response to tail pinch', both of which describe a conscious, pinch-responsive, fully recovering mouse. O'Rourke rodent IT - grade 3 begins at 4, which the authors define in words as 'Hind paws don't move - full hindlimb paralysis' (the paper's own text: 'By 3 h, peak scores of 4 were reached (full tail, hindlimb, and hind paw paralysis)'), NOT at 3 'Hind limbs don't support weight, but can still move'. Bravo-Hernandez rat aA - 5 is 'Severe vocalizations', 6 is 'Any type of tremors or seizure', 7 is 'Death'; the NHP scale's 7 is 'Euthanasia required', and several rows wrongly attribute that wording to the rat scale. Only two scales in this batch survive intact, and both survive because their top band is DEFINED as death or euthanasia: Hagedorn, where 20 is 'severe signs in all categories, including convulsions resulting in euthanasia' (11 rows, all confirmed), and Moazami EvADINT, where 75 is the score automatically assigned to a mouse that died. The rule to propagate to the ~145 unchecked grade-3 rows: grade 3 only where the recorded value denotes death, euthanasia, unresponsiveness/moribundity or frank paralysis in the SOURCE'S wording, and grep notes for 'Grade mapping for' to find the rest.

2. REVERSIBILITY IS RECORDED AND THEN IGNORED. Every downgraded acute row already carries reversibility=reversible and quotes the paper saying so - O'Rourke: 'reversed within 24 h with no sequelae' and 'By 16-24 h and for the next 2 weeks, all animals scored a 0'; Bravo-Hernandez: 'peaking 15 min after ON dosing and resolving after 120 min' with 'no apparent sequelae'; Moazami: 'Even severely affected mice, unless they died, recovered fully by 24 h'. The rubric's grade 1 explicitly covers 'transient acute behavioural signs resolving within hours-days'. A row whose own reversibility field says reversible and whose value is below the scale's death/unresponsiveness band is a downgrade candidate on sight - no re-fetch needed to triage them.

3. GRADE 3 ON readout_value = TBD. 16 rows in this batch carry TBD and a grade inferred from prose. The test that separates them is whether the SOURCE states a qualifying outcome in words AT THE CITED LOCUS. Four pass and keep grade 3: CMS1874 (O'Rourke 1000 ug IT, 'both posterior and anterior regions were impacted' with the heat map legend reading 'paresis/paralysis'), CMS1653 (Kuroda rat IT, 'revealed increased scores, including severe paraplegia'), CMS1992 (Korte group 2, 'in two-third it required euthanasia') and CMS1232 (Spinraza SmPC, 'Some patients were implanted with a ventriculo-peritoneal shunt'). The rest fail and were downgraded. Note the two failure shapes: a conditional class-level sentence ('If severe enough, this ... can be a dose-limiting finding in NHP' - CMS1982) and a generic higher-dose sentence with no group attached ('including prolonged and fatal seizures' - CMS1957, CMS1985).

4. THE IN VITRO PARENT-COMPARATOR INVERSION IS STILL LIVE, AND IT IS NOW FIVE ROWS. CMS2052, CMS2057, CMS2058, CMS2060 and CMS2061 are BE(2)-M17 viability/LDH rows at 20 nM, 72 h, all with readout_value=TBD, all graded 3, and all with effect_vs_control phrased against the PARENT ASO2 - while the figures they cite normalise to vehicle ('shown as the mean percentage relative to vehicle'). Two of them are PS-3(-), the variant that in the SAME paper had the lowest in vivo mortality of the three PO variants (1/5) and 'exhibited reduced late-onset neurotoxicity'; they were graded above variants that killed 2/5, 3/5 and 4/4. CMS2052 states its reason outright - 'Graded 3 because the matched in vivo arm was programme-limiting' - importing another experiment's outcome into an in vitro row. Sweep the whole in vitro lane for effect_vs_control containing 'vs parent', 'than parent' or 'worsened ... vs': no in vitro cytotoxicity row should carry grade 3 at all under this rubric.

5. HISTOPATHOLOGY THAT CONTRADICTS THE GRADE - KURODA. The paper twice states the opposite of degeneration: 'Histopathological analysis of the lumbar cord, cerebellum, and hippocampus revealed no neuronal cell death or inflammation for either ASO, indicating that severe neurodegeneration or gliosis cannot explain in vivo late-onset neurological dysfunction by ASO2', and 'Our histopathological analysis showed no neuronal cell death in CNS tissues of rats exhibiting lethal toxicity in neurobehavioral tests'. Both facts belong in the dataset. The consequence for grading is narrow but firm: the mortality rows keep grade 3 because death is death, but no Kuroda row may be graded 3 on a degeneration reading, and the functional rows (tolerability score, open-field speed, bladder volume) have no grade-3 limb left.

6. ONE CLINICAL EVENT SPREAD OVER SEVERAL GRADE-3 ROWS. Kuroda's single rat IT experiment yields four rows - tolerability score, open-field speed, bladder volume and mortality - and all four were graded 3 off the same paraplegia-plus-one-death narrative; the KCNT1 hydrocephalus event appears three times (CMS1613, CMS1619 primary, plus CMS1640, a review restatement whose own notes admit it 'intentionally DUPLICATES' them); CMS1567 and CMS1568 describe the same 13 Wave patients. For a model learning what severe neurotoxicity looks like this multiplies single events. Grade each row from its OWN readout, and flag the class-level and duplicate rows (CMS1982 and the four Korte rows attach to no identifiable oligonucleotide, with dose, duration and value all TBD).

7. MEASUREMENT_IDs ARE NOT STABLE ACROSS BATCH SNAPSHOTS, AND ONE EARLIER CORRECTION LANDED ON THE WRONG ROW. Eight ids appear in both batch_grade3.json and batch_grade3_journals.json with DIFFERENT content (CMS1666, CMS1866, CMS1874, CMS1907, CMS1922, CMS1931, CMS1939, CMS2061); data/cns_measurements.csv matches the newer journals snapshot. Two further CSV defects surfaced while cross-checking: CMS1985's readout_value is the literal string '3.75 (or keep TBD)' - a sentence written into a numeric cell - and CMS1942's readout_value was silently changed from 4.0 to 3.75 without the row's source_table note being updated. 8. THE BATCH IS MIS-LABELLED: 8 OF ITS 76 ROWS ARE NOT JOURNAL ARTICLES. CMS1168 (EMA Qalsody SmPC/EPAR), CMS1199 and CMS1201 (FDA TEGSEDI label), CMS1227, CMS1228, CMS1231 (Biogen DHPC + MHRA Drug Safety Update) and CMS1232 (EMA Spinraza SmPC) are regulatory or grey-literature rows, and CMS1992-CMS1995 rest on a paywalled abstract. 9. RIGHTS: ONE OVER-CLAIM, THREE ROWS. CMS1227, CMS1228 and CMS1231 are filed public_domain on the strength of a Biogen Direct Healthcare Professional Communication plus an MHRA Drug Safety Update. A manufacturer's DHPC is not a public-domain document and MHRA output is UK Crown copyright under the Open Government Licence; the schema's public_domain means US patents and FDA/EMA documents. Set them to verify. The rest of the batch's rights check out: Kuroda, Hagedorn and Moazami are correctly cc_by, and O'Rourke and Bravo-Hernandez are CC BY-NC and correctly held at summary_stat.

10. BAR-CHART DIGITISATION IS PRODUCING IMPOSSIBLE NUMBERS. Every O'Rourke Fig. 5C/5E and Fig. 3B value and every Bravo-Hernandez Fig. 1F value is read off a bar chart; the papers publish no numeric group means. With n=4 per group on an integer 0-7 scale the mean must be a multiple of 0.25, yet the batch contains 4.4, 4.9, 5.1, 5.3, 6.2 and 6.4 - none attainable. The grade conclusions are unaffected here (4.4/4.9/5.1 are below 6 either way; 6.2/6.4 round to 6.25/6.5, still above), but the false precision should be removed: either round to the attainable grid or use TBD and keep the qualitative finding, as the extractor already did for CMS1874. Related: effect_vs_control for the whole Fig. 5C/5E block asserts 'vs 0 in PBS-injected controls', but Supplementary Table 13 tabulates only PS-vs-PO comparisons for those panels - the PBS comparator is not published at that locus and should not be stated as if it were.
